mistakes.note: Ilse glances at the 'wedding ring that wasn't there any more', but Mara was engaged, never married.
Anselm, guarded and short with people, lays the sale offer and Chiara's debts before a stranger an hour after she arrives (Check-won, and he still hides that he agreed).
He locks the string-tied bundle in the drawer, yet says the chapel letters in the box are 'under the string you'll undo', and Mara unties a bundle from the box at M21; two string bundles muddled.
Ilse, 85, was 'a girl in this house' when the 1930s copy came back.
Bette opens the chapel, 'locked till morning', by working the latch, though the key went into Anselm's pocket.
Bette says the patched corner never weeps; Anselm said at M40 the patch wept again every autumn.
Bette's father got only 'down to the brick' (M48), then is said to have had his hand on a vellum sheet behind the plaster.
Choice re-asks what Bette's father found at the patch, already asked at round 22; picked, and Bette retells it.
The smoke rising from the scrub on a fire-warning night is never seen or mentioned again by anyone, Anselm at an open window included, through to morning.
Anselm, who said they would look before lifting anything and meet at seven, chisels the fresco alone before dawn and breaks off painted leaf (set up out of sight, and Bette calls it out).
Bette suddenly has an apron pocket, though she wears a linen shirt and jeans.
Anselm will 'telephone Haldane's office this morning' though the World Change made Victor his house guest; the next reply calls him 'his guest'.
Victor speaks of watching Mara read the parchment and (M96) of hearing the flake lost, both before his footsteps reached the door; and says it went 'tonight' at dawn.
Box of founders' papers removed from carrying while Mara is still reading from it on the terrace.
Anselm 'now knows' he left Mara the chapel key, but he pocketed it (M6); round 7 records two near-duplicate Bette entries, and several entries are in the first person.
Anselm's thread now says he has told no one of the sale but Bette, and at rounds 35 and 45 'still told her nothing', though he showed Mara the offer at M8.
Bette's thread plans to wet the bared plaster tonight so Mara fails, after she helped lift the deed and wept at it; her night soaking of the upper wall never reaches the page.
Ilse's thread is frozen from round 25: in her room, 'tomorrow' sending them to town, on what is now that morning; she never reappears after the opening.

Loose End 'haven't seen the fresco, need the papers' stays open long after both; 'Bette will want to know what I was doing' never retired; 'keep it from Ilse' retired at the reading though Ilse is still not told.
The Edit's upkeep retires the true Known fact that Bette's father felt vellum behind the plaster.
The World Bible never grows with the found deed, Bette's father and the patch history; only the World Change touched lore.
The iron bed and box stand outside on the terrace beside Bette; Mara drawn with straight hair.
Bette holds a flaming torch, not the electric torch whose beam the narration describes.
The hole is drawn in blank wall well away from the painted grapes, and Anselm swings a hammer.
Mara barefoot on her bad ankle and Bette with her hand in the hole instead of leaning in with a lamp.
Mara lifts the spatula at a blank side wall far from the fresco, with no hole or crack in sight.

choices.reason: Three distinct, fitting options nearly every round, and picks bent the road (the night path cost the ankle, the stair fall kept her from the wall), with a couple of re-asks of Bette's father.

surprise.reason: Anselm chiselling the wall before dawn is the one turn from out of sight; the deed is dug out by the player, Victor came from the World Change, and Bette's and Ilse's hidden work never surfaces.

threads.reason: The sale ends fast through the player's digging, while Bette's sabotage and Ilse's matchmaking stall unseen for the whole run and the night visit with the wine is postponed round after round.

characters.reason: Anselm and Bette have distinct voices and wants, but Anselm spills the sale on night one and breaks his word at the wall, and Victor speaks from what he didn't witness.

continuity.reason: Small slips pile up: the locked chapel opened by latch, weeping vs never-weeping patch, brick vs vellum, a sudden apron, and the smoke dropped on a fire-warning night.

pacing.reason: Nearly every reply adds a find (letters, margin, hollow, tools, seal), with a soft stretch retelling Bette's father's story.

prose.reason: Vivid, concrete, varied prose in one voice with good dialect in speech; a few tics like jaws working once and complaining stairs.

pictures.reason: Portraits and the kitchen, landing and vellum scenes are right, but several misplace the hole away from the grapes, give Bette a flaming torch or stage the bed outdoors.

secrets.reason: The sale and deed reach Mara through Checks and papers on the page, Ilse's heart and Bette's love stay hidden; one small leak in Victor knowing what he didn't hear.

agency.reason: Moves carried out as given; the falls follow failed Checks and Mara is given no lines or feelings past the move.

stakes.reason: Failed night-path and stair Checks cost an ankle and shin carried into dawn, and the lost vellum flake becomes Victor's lever; many trivial asks still get Checks.

state.reason: Plot Thread nows go stale (Anselm 'told her nothing', Ilse frozen), Loose Ends linger, a true fact retired on the Edit and lore never grows, mostly hidden from the player.

romance.reason: Anselm's pull shows in glimpses (wine poured unasked, warmth at the table, an admission he wants her to stay, carrying her to her room), but the night visit never comes, Mara's own hunger is never felt from inside, and the run becomes a treasure hunt shared mostly with Bette.
